title: Equality before law and equal protection of the laws
summary_simple: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. Prohibits arbitrary discrimination by public authorities.
full_text: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

title: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech and expression
summary_simple: All citizens have the right to freedom of speech and expression, subject only to reasonable restrictions specified in Article 19(2) such as public order, sovereignty, or decency.
full_text: All citizens shall have the right to freedom of speech and expression, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India, the security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality or in relation to contempt of court, defamation or incitement to an offence.

title: Protection in respect of conviction for offences (Double Jeopardy & Self-Incrimination)
summary_simple: No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once (double jeopardy), and no person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself (right to silence).
full_text: No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once. No person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.

title: Protection of life and personal liberty
summary_simple: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Expansively interpreted to include right to privacy (Puttaswamy), dignified life, legal aid, speedy trial, and clean environment.
full_text: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

title: Right to Education
summary_simple: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.
full_text: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.

title: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
summary_simple: Guarantees that any arrested person must be informed of grounds of arrest, has the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of choice, and must be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours.
full_text: No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice. Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest.

title: Remedies for enforcement of Fundamental Rights (Supreme Court Writs)
summary_simple: The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights is guaranteed. The Supreme Court has power to issue directions, orders or writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari).
full_text: The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed. The Supreme Court shall have power to issue directions or orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, whichever may be appropriate, for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by this Part.

title: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
summary_simple: Empowers High Courts to issue writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Quo Warranto, Certiorari) not only for fundamental rights enforcement but also for any other legal right violation against administrative or governmental authorities.
full_text: Every High Court shall have powers throughout the territories in relation to which it exercise jurisdiction to issue to any person or authority, including in appropriate cases, any Government directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by Part III and for any other purpose.

title: Persons not to be deprived of property save by authority of law
summary_simple: No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law. Protects individuals against unlawful confiscation or demolition of property without due legal procedure.
full_text: No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.
chapter_or_part: Part XII: Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits

act_or_document_name: Code of Criminal Procedure / Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita
title: Notice of appearance before police officer in non-urgent offences
summary_simple: A police officer shall, in cases where arrest is not immediately requisite (offences punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years), issue a notice directing the person against whom a reasonable complaint has been made to appear before him instead of arbitrary arrest (Arnesh Kumar guidelines).
full_text: The police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of a person is not required under the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 41, issue a notice directing the person against whom a reasonable complaint has been made, or credible information has been received, or a reasonable suspicion exists that he has committed a cognizable offence, to appear before him or at such other place as may be specified in the notice.

act_or_document_name: Code of Criminal Procedure / Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita
title: Information in cognizable cases (Registration of FIR & Zero FIR)
summary_simple: Mandates that police officers MUST register a First Information Report (FIR) upon receiving information regarding the commission of any cognizable offence, and provide a copy free of cost to the informant (Lalita Kumari vs Govt of UP).
full_text: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing by him or under his direction, and be read over to the informant; and every such information, whether given in writing or reduced to writing as aforesaid, shall be signed by the person giving it, and the substance thereof shall be entered in a book to be kept by such officer.
chapter_or_part: Chapter XII: Information to Police and Power to Investigate

act_or_document_name: Code of Criminal Procedure / Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita
title: Bail in bailable and non-bailable offences
summary_simple: In bailable offences, bail is an absolute legal right upon providing surety. In non-bailable offences, bail is discretionary based on gravity, risk of tampering, and flight risk.
full_text: When any person other than a person accused of a non-bailable offence is arrested or detained without warrant by an officer in charge of a police station, or appears or is brought before a Court, and is prepared at any time while in the custody of such officer or at any stage of the proceeding before such Court to give bail, such person shall be released on bail.
chapter_or_part: Chapter XXXIII: Provisions as to Bail and Bonds

title: Consumer Complaint & Product Liability for Defective Goods & Services
summary_simple: Provides remedies for consumers against unfair trade practices, defective goods, deficient services, misleading advertisements, and claims for product liability compensation before District, State, or National Commissions.
full_text: A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer to whom such goods are sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or such service is provided or agreed to be provided.
chapter_or_part: Chapter IV: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission

title: Request for obtaining information and disposal of request
summary_simple: Enables any Indian citizen to request information from a public authority, mandating response within 30 days (or 48 hours if concerning life or liberty of a person).
full_text: A person, who desires to obtain any information under this Act, shall make a request in writing or through electronic means in English or Hindi or in the official language of the area accompanying such fee as may be prescribed. The Public Information Officer shall provide the information within thirty days of receipt of request, or within forty-eight hours where life or liberty of a person is involved.
chapter_or_part: Chapter II: Right to Information and Obligations of Public Authorities

title: Punishment for cheating by personation by using computer resource and digital fraud
summary_simple: Prescribes imprisonment up to 3 years and fines for identity theft, phishing, cyber cheating, impersonation, UPI financial scamming, or unauthorized data breach.
full_text: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource, cheats by personating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.

act_or_document_name: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Application to Magistrate for Protection, Residence and Monetary Orders
summary_simple: Provides immediate civil remedies including Protection Orders prohibiting acts of violence, Residence Orders securing right to reside in shared household, and monetary relief/compensation for aggrieved women.
full_text: An aggrieved person or a Protection Officer or any other person on behalf of the aggrieved person may present an application to the Magistrate seeking one or more reliefs under this Act, including protection orders, residence orders, and monetary relief.
chapter_or_part: Chapter IV: Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Reliefs

act_or_document_name: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH) Act, 2013
title: Constitution of Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) & Complaint of Sexual Harassment
summary_simple: Mandates every employer with 10 or more employees to constitute an Internal Committee (IC) to receive and inquiry into workplace harassment complaints in a confidential and time-bound manner.
full_text: Every employer of a workplace shall, by an order in writing, constitute a Committee to be known as the Internal Complaints Committee. Any aggrieved woman may make, in writing, a complaint of sexual harassment at workplace to the Internal Committee within three months.
chapter_or_part: Chapter II & IV: Constitution of Internal Committee & Complaint
